chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Rifāʿah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
If the ground is wet, with neither dust in it nor water, then look for the driest place you can find and perform tayammum from it, for that is an easing from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
He said: If he is in snow, then let him look at the felt of his saddle and perform tayammum from its dust, or from something dusty.
And if he is in a condition where he finds nothing but clay, then there is no harm in performing tayammum from it.

key_terms.أَجَفَّ: the driest, meaning the least wet place available
key_terms.الطِّينَ: clay or mud, which may be used for tayammum when nothing else is found
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: the ground or earth used here as the surface from which tayammum is sought
key_terms.تَوْسِيعٌ: an easing or expansion, indicating Divine facilitation
key_terms.ثَلْجٍ: snow, a condition in which ordinary earth may be inaccessible
key_terms.غُبَارِهِ: its dust, referring to dust found on the saddle felt or similar object
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum, the dry ablution in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.مُبْتَلَّةً: wet or moistened, describing ground unsuitable in the normal manner

ai.seo_question: How should tayammum be performed when the ground is wet, snowy, or only clay is available?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the rulings of tayammum when normal materials for purification are difficult to access, such as on wet ground, in snow, or when only clay is available. It shows the facilitation in the Sacred Law, allowing tayammum from the driest available place, from dust on equipment, or even from clay in cases of necessity.
